newsitem.title: USA: Phillips building Belgium plastics facility.
newsitem.headline: Phillips building Belgium plastics facility.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Wednesday it is building a Ryton PPS (polyphenylene sulfide) compounding facility near Antwerp, Belgium.
Cost of the facility, scheduled for completion by April 1, 1997, was not disclosed.
After it is completed, Phillips will move its entire plastics laboratory, and its Ryton customer and technical services divisions to Antwerp from Overijse, Belgium.
Ryton is an engineering plastic known for its heat and chemical resistance, as well as its ability to be molded to tight tolerances.
Its applications include electronic components, under-the-hood automotive parts and appliances.
Compounding is the combining of Ryton PPS with glass fibers or mineral fillers to tailor the engineering plastic to customer needs.
Initially, the Antwerp facility will be capable of producing 8.4 million pounds a year of compounded Ryton PPS, Phillips said. The plant is expandable to approximately 30 million pounds a year.
